source: Written for Wayword as a learner's guide; not part of the original dataset. Examples are dataset phrases.
intro: Russian spelling is fairly regular once you know which syllable is stressed. Stress changes how the vowels sound, so learn it along with each word.
reading: CAPITALS mark the stress. Russian stress can fall anywhere and isn't marked in normal writing.
"y" on its own (vy, ty, byl) means the ы sound, not "why".
"yeh", "nyet" and "gdyeh" mean the consonant is soft (see below).

sounds.symbol: Р Н В С У Х
sounds.name: Letters that lie
sounds.spelled: r, n, v, s, oo, kh
sounds.how: They look like Latin letters but sound different: Р = r, Н = n, В = v, С = s, У = oo, Х = kh. Also Е = ye and Я = ya.

sounds.name: Yery
sounds.how: Start saying "ee", then pull your tongue back and relax your lips. It sits between the i in "bit" and the u in "put".

sounds.symbol: ь  е ё и ю я
sounds.name: Soft consonants
sounds.how: Before these letters, a consonant is made with the middle of your tongue raised, which adds a faint y: Нет is "nyet", not "net".

sounds.name: Unstressed O
sounds.how: An o that isn't stressed sounds like "ah", or a weak "uh" further from the stress. Only the stressed о sounds like "oh".

sounds.name: Unstressed E / Ya
sounds.how: When they aren't stressed, е and я shrink toward a short "ee": дела is "dee-LAH".

sounds.name: Kha
sounds.how: Like the ch in Scottish "loch", but softer than the Arabic or Hebrew sound.

sounds.name: Er
sounds.how: A tapped or lightly rolled r made with the tip of the tongue, as in Spanish or Italian.

sounds.name: Hushing sounds
sounds.how: ж = zh as in "measure", ш = a hard sh, щ = a longer, softer sh (shch), ч = ch. Exception: in что, ч is said as sh ("shtoh").

sounds.name: Final devoicing
sounds.how: At the end of a word, or before a voiceless consonant, voiced letters turn voiceless: д sounds like t, в like f.

tips_source: "How it's said" tips are written for Wayword (not part of the dataset): how a native Russian speaker says the phrase at normal speed, next to the careful pronunciation line.

tips.good_morning: The endings are weak and quick: DOH-bruh-yuh OO-truh.
tips.how_are_you: The k of как turns into a g before the d of дела, so it comes out kag dee-LAH.
tips.please: In everyday speech the -уй- in the middle drops out: pah-ZHAHL-stuh. In a hurry it can shrink to just pzhahl-stuh.
tips.thank_you: The final o is a weak "uh": spah-SEE-buh.
tips.dont_speak_well: Only the syllable just before the stress keeps a clear "ah"; the one before that shrinks to "uh": guh-vah-RYOO. Русски has just one s sound: pah-ROO-skee.
tips.dont_understand: Не attaches to the verb like one long word, and the first o of понимаю is weak: ya nee-puh-nee-MAH-yoo.
tips.learning_language: Русский has just one s sound, despite the double letter: ya oo-CHOO ROO-skee.
tips.where_is: Где is a single syllable: the g and d go straight together, with no vowel in between.
tips.bathroom: Туа slides into one syllable, "twah": gdyeh twah-LYET.
tips.how_get: Как becomes kag before the d, and -ться is said as one ts sound: kag dah-BRAH-tsuh dah.
tips.is_far: Это's final o is weak, and the first syllable of далеко shrinks to "duh": EH-tuh duh-lee-KOH.
tips.how_much: The final o's are weak "uh" sounds: SKOL-kuh EH-tuh STOH-eet.
tips.bill: Most people say сч as one long, soft sh, without a clear ch in it: something like sh-shyot.
tips.thanks_help: The final щ is a long, soft sh, and the second o is weak: spah-SEE-buh zah POH-muhsh.
tips.what_do_you_do: The ш and с of -шься merge into one long sh, and за is weak: chem ty zuh-nee-MAH-yesh-shuh.
tips.nice_meeting: -ться is one ts sound, and the first o of познакомиться is weak: pree-YAHT-nuh puhz-nah-KOH-mee-tsuh.
tips.like_talking: -тся in нравится is one ts sound, and the first syllable of разговаривать shrinks: mnyeh NRAH-vee-tsuh s tah-BOY ruhz-gah-VAH-ree-vuht.
